title: Scalar extension of the tangent module of an augmented smooth algebra
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $B$ a smooth commutative $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and $u:B\to A$ an $A$-algebra homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Give $A$ the $B$-module structure through $u$, and write $T(B,u)=\operatorname{Der}_A(B,A)$, the $A$-module of additive maps $d:B\to A$ satisfying $d(ab)=a\,d(b)$ for $a\in A$, $d(A)=0$ and $d(bb')=u(b)d(b')+u(b')d(b)$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Then $T(B,u)$ is finite projective, meaning a direct summand of $A^n$ for some finite $n$. For every homomorphism $f:A\to C$ of commutative rings put $B_C=C\otimes_A B$, with its tensor-product algebra structure [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], and $u_C(c\otimes b)=c f(u(b))$. There is a canonical $C$-linear isomorphism
$$\theta_C:C\otimes_A T(B,u)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(B_C,u_C),\qquad \theta_C(c\otimes d)(c'\otimes b)=cc'f(d(b)),$$
where tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and the target consists of $C$-derivations into $C$ through $u_C$. For $A\to C\xrightarrow h D$, the comparison for $A\to D$ equals the composite comparison for $A\to C$ and $C\to D$ under $D\otimes_C(C\otimes_A T)\simeq D\otimes_A T$, $d_0\otimes(c\otimes v)\mapsto d_0h(c)\otimes v$; the identity comparison is the identity. The comparison is natural in augmented smooth algebras: if $v:B'\to A$ is another such augmentation and $q:B\to B'$ is an $A$-algebra homomorphism with $v q=u$, precomposition $T(B',v)\to T(B,u)$ commutes with every $\theta_C$. Neither $A$ nor $C$ is required to be Noetherian or nonzero, and $C$ is not required to be flat over $A$.

source.place: Tags 00T2 (definition-smooth), 00RO (lemma-universal-omega), 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change). The augmented tangent comparison and its naturality are the finite-projective dual consequence of these statements; the assembly argument is recorded in report.md, not asserted verbatim in Stacks.

proof.text: Put $\Omega=\Omega_{B/A}$ and $P=A\otimes_{B,u}\Omega$. Smoothness [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] says that there are $B$-linear maps $i:\Omega\to B^n$ and $p:B^n\to\Omega$ with $pi=1$. Applying $A\otimes_{B,u}(-)$ preserves this equation by the functoriality in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The coordinate maps $a\otimes(b_j)_j\mapsto(a u(b_j))_j$ identify $A\otimes_B B^n$ with $A^n$, with inverse $(a_j)_j\mapsto\sum_j a_j\otimes e_j$. Thus $P$ is a direct summand of $A^n$. The algebra tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], applied to $1_C$ and $f u$, gives the augmentation $u_C(c\otimes b)=cf(u(b))$.

source.place: Tag 00T2 (definition-smooth); tensor universal property and explicit split maps

proof.text: The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] identifies $T(B,u)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_B(\Omega,A)$, with $B$ acting on $A$ through $u$. This is $P^*=\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,A)$: the mutually inverse correspondences are $\ell\mapsto(a\otimes\omega\mapsto a\ell(\omega))$ and $\lambda\mapsto(\omega\mapsto\lambda(1\otimes\omega))$. The first is balanced since $\ell(b\omega)=u(b)\ell(\omega)$; the tensor universal property proves that these formulas are linear and inverse. In particular, $d\in T(B,u)$ corresponds to $\lambda_d$ with $\lambda_d(1\otimes\mathrm db)=d(b)$. The identical argument for $C,B_C,u_C$ gives $T(B_C,u_C)=P_C^*$, where $P_C=C\otimes_{B_C,u_C}\Omega_{B_C/C}$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] to $A\to C$ and $A\to B$. It gives the $B_C$-linear isomorphism $B_C\otimes_B\Omega\simeq\Omega_{B_C/C}$ sending $(c\otimes b_0)\otimes\mathrm db$ to $(c\otimes b_0)\mathrm d(1\otimes b)$. Tensor its inverse with $C$ through $u_C$. The remaining balanced tensor identifications give an isomorphism $\alpha_C:C\otimes_A P\simeq P_C$, with $c\otimes(a\otimes\omega)\mapsto cf(a)\otimes\eta(\omega)$, where $\eta(\mathrm db)=\mathrm d(1\otimes b)$. Explicitly, the inverse before the differential identification sends $c\otimes((c_0\otimes b_0)\otimes\omega)$ to $cc_0\otimes(u(b_0)\otimes\omega)$. The balancing relations for $B,A,C$ verify both composites. Consequently $\alpha_C(c\otimes(1\otimes\mathrm db))=c\otimes\mathrm d(1\otimes b)$.

source.place: Tag 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change); tensoring an isomorphism and balanced cancellation

proof.text: By [lem-sf-finite-projective-dual], $P^*$ is finite projective ($P$ is a summand of $A^n$ by step 1); through step 2 this proves the first assertion about $T(B,u)$. For an $A$-module $M$ put $M^*=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,A)$ and define $\beta_M:C\otimes_AM^*\to\operatorname{Hom}_C(C\otimes_AM,C)$ by $\beta_M(c\otimes\lambda)(c_1\otimes x)=cc_1f(\lambda(x))$. The inner formula is $A$-balanced since $f(\lambda(ax))=f(a)f(\lambda(x))$, and the outer one since $cf(a)\otimes\lambda$ and $c\otimes a\lambda$ give the same functional; so the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] makes $\beta_M$ a well-defined $C$-linear map. For an $A$-linear $g:M\to N$, with $g^*(\mu)=\mu g$, both $\beta_M(1_C\otimes g^*)$ and $(1_C\otimes g)^*\beta_N$ send $c\otimes\mu$ to $c_1\otimes x\mapsto cc_1f(\mu(g(x)))$. For $M=A^n$ the elements $1\otimes e_j^*$ form a $C$-basis of $C\otimes_A(A^n)^*$, the elements $1\otimes e_k$ a $C$-basis of $C\otimes_AA^n$, and $\beta_{A^n}(1\otimes e_j^*)(1\otimes e_k)=\delta_{jk}$, so $\beta_{A^n}$ is an isomorphism, also for $n=0$. With $i:P\to A^n$, $p:A^n\to P$, $pi=1$ from step 1, put $\gamma=(1_C\otimes i^*)\beta_{A^n}^{-1}(1_C\otimes p)^*$. Naturality for $i$ gives $\beta_P\gamma=(1\otimes i)^*(1\otimes p)^*=(1\otimes pi)^*=1$; naturality for $p$, $(1\otimes p)^*\beta_P=\beta_{A^n}(1\otimes p^*)$, gives $\gamma\beta_P=1\otimes(pi)^*=1$. So $\beta_P:C\otimes_AP^*\simeq(C\otimes_AP)^*$ is an isomorphism, with $(c\otimes\lambda)(c_1\otimes x)=cc_1f(\lambda(x))$; no flatness of $C$ is used. Compose this with precomposition by $\alpha_C^{-1}$ and the two identifications of step 2. This defines the canonical $C$-linear isomorphism $\theta_C$. On $1\otimes\mathrm d(1\otimes b)=\alpha_C(1\otimes(1\otimes\mathrm db))$ the resulting functional has value $c f(d(b))$. Since a $C$-derivation vanishes on $C$, its value at $c_1\otimes b=c_1(1\otimes b)$ is therefore $cc_1f(d(b))$, exactly the asserted formula.

source.place: Tag 07VI (lemma-dual-perfect-complex), degree-zero finite-projective duality; scalar formula from the cited calculus node

proof.text: For $A\xrightarrow f C\xrightarrow h D$, identify $D\otimes_C B_C$ with $D\otimes_A B$ by $d_0\otimes(c\otimes b)\mapsto d_0h(c)\otimes b$; the inverse sends $d_0\otimes b$ to $d_0\otimes(1\otimes b)$, and these maps preserve augmentation. Evaluate the successive comparisons on $d_0\otimes(c\otimes v)$ and on an algebra generator $d_1\otimes b$. Their value is $d_0d_1h(c)h(f(v(b)))$. The direct comparison after the asserted tensor associator has the same value. Additivity and the tensor universal property give equality on all elements. For $C=A$ the formula is $\theta_A(a\otimes v)(a_1\otimes b)=aa_1v(b)$, so multiplication identifies it with $av$ and makes the comparison the identity.

source.place: Tensor universal property; explicit identity and composition calculation

proof.text: Let $q:B\to B^{\prime}$ satisfy $v q=u$. Precomposition sends $d^{\prime}$ to $d^{\prime}q$: its product rule uses $v(q(b))=u(b)$, so it is a derivation through $u$. The scalar extension is $q_C(c_1\otimes b)=c_1\otimes q(b)$ and satisfies $v_C q_C=u_C$. Both composites in the naturality square, on $c\otimes d^{\prime}$ evaluated at $c_1\otimes b$, give $cc_1 f(d^{\prime}(q(b)))$. Pure tensors generate both tensor modules, hence the square commutes. All constructions used split equations or tensor universal properties, never exactness of tensoring. They apply to the zero ring and to nonflat $A\to C$ as well.
